thread.title: Trump's China tariff announcement criticized by association including 22 Dow company CEOs - MarketWatch

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Trump's China tariff announcement criticized by association including 22 Dow company CEOs - MarketWatch
text: The Business Roundtable, an association of chief executive officers that promotes pro-economic and business public policies, criticized President Donald Trump's announcement of tariffs on Chinese products totaling up to $60 billion. The Business Roundtable's members include CEOs of 22 of 30 Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -1.42% components, including Apple Inc.'s AAPL, +0.14% Tim Cook, Boeing Co.'s BA, -2.76% Dennis Muilenburg, Exxon Mobil Corp.'s XOM, -1.17% Darren Woods, General Electric Co.'s GE, -1.98% John Flannery and J.P. Morgan Chase & Co.'s JPM, -2.30% Jamie Dimon. BR said in a statement: "Unilaterally imposing tariffs or other restrictions without a long-term strategy to bring about reforms in China will only raise prices in America, make American companies and products less competitive, and harm U.S. workers and consumers." Instead, BR recommended an approach centered around several strategic priorities, including working with international partners to identify unfair trade barriers and practices that China must remove, setting deadlines for reforms and outlining actions the U.S. will take if the reforms aren't undertaken.
